procedure.step: Register the factory through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service (moet.gov.ae) before applying for a certificate; registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added, and takes about three working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Apply for a preferential Certificate of Origin for India via the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter the factory's purchase invoice), pay the fee online, submit the application, and receive approval or a return with comments to correct; then print the approved certificate.
Pay the certificate fee of AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000) as charged by the Ministry of Foreign Trade.

The certificate is issued prior to, at, or within five working days of export, is valid for twelve months from the date of issue, and covers only one import (it may list several products). It must bear the authorised signature and official seal of the competent authority.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020 including which origin criterion is claimed, keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing, and must answer a customs request within ten working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

The goods must be shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. An invoice issued by a third party does not by itself cause the claim to be denied, but the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Indian inputs count as originating only with proof of their originating status (bilateral cumulation, Art. 3.7).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

Only for a certificate issued retrospectively: the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
Assumes the certificate's invoice value equals the shipment value given.
